title: Smarter escalation routing with trace-linked runbooks
creator: Samir Patel
description: Problem: When SLO/alert noise occurs, oncall responders spend time triaging basic signal (trace/span signature, common logs) before finding the canonical runbook. This increases time-to-detection and MTTR. Goal: Build an automated mapping layer that matches incoming traces & log signatures to the most relevant runbook and uses that mapping to route PagerDuty escalations adaptively. Deliverables: trace-runbook mapping service, Slack action buttons to launch runbook steps, PagerDuty routing rules that include alternate responders based on historical availability, automated postmortem draft generator pre-populated with trace snippets and timeline. Success criteria: 20% reduction in median MTTR for infra and runtime incidents in next quarter; >90% precision on runbook selection in staging; safe rollout path with feature flag and canary on non-critical services. Out of scope: full NLP-based root cause inference and integration with third-party runbook managers for initial rollout.
tasks: [ ] Define runbook signature schema (trace fingerprints, top N error logs, metric delta patterns)
[ ] Implement lightweight trace-indexer service that emits signatures for new traces
[ ] Create mapping UI in Console for mapping signatures to runbooks (PM/Design review required)
[ ] Add PagerDuty adaptive routing rules and matching webhook to our ops-layer
[ ] Implement Slack action buttons and ephemeral modals to surface runbook steps
[ ] Auto-generate postmortem draft with timeline, top traces, and logs and attach to Linear incident ticket
[ ] Add feature flag + canary rollout plan and load test for signature throughput
[ ] E2E tests (synthetic incidents), security review, and runbook authoring playbook
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created after oncall retrospective — multiple incidents wasted 15-30m on runbook discovery.
2026-02-18: Sig schema draft complete; engineering + SRE alignment session. Decided on 5-tuple: service, top-span-op, dominant-exception, metric-name, anomaly-window.
2026-02-25: Initial prototype of trace-indexer implemented (collector hook + signature emitter). Produces stable IDs for common failure modes.
2026-03-02: Design handed off for mapping UI. PM requested capability to attach alternate runbooks and annotation fields for escalation guidance.
2026-03-05: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4521 — trace-indexer + signature matcher. Unit tests passing; needs integration tests.

2026-03-08: PagerDuty routing proposal reviewed with SRE. Agreed on staged rollout: only non-prod and low-sev prod alerts in first wave. Added fallback to oncall schedule + backup responders based on recent ack latency.
2026-03-10: QA found mismatch cases where signatures collide across services; mitigation: add service-scoped priority and manual override in Console mapping UI. Updated estimate + plan.
Next: finalize security review, add postmortem generator template, and schedule canary for 2026-03-18.
notes: Trade-offs: Compact signature favors precision and low compute cost but may miss compound failures. We will iterate with additional features if precision <90% in staging.
Privacy: traces and logs attached to postmortem drafts must be scrubbed of PII before persistence; follow data-retention policy.
Rollout safety: feature flag gates on team and service; PagerDuty changes require ops review and will be reversible via runbook mapping UI.
Follow-ups: Evaluate ML-based clustering of signatures after 2 quarters to reduce manual mapping maintenance.
